findings.title: Fresh CI check reads a historical attempt without checking the current run
findings.body: A later rerun can leave attempt 1 successful while the current run is pending or failed. Query actions/runs/RUN as well and require the current run_attempt to be 1, completed and successful before using the attempt-1 job evidence.

findings.title: Pause is not checked before each new subprocess/API read
findings.body: A reset during the preflight/read sequence permits further network reads and evidence writes until the next coarse pause_guard. Put a pause check in command/API wrappers and keep any exception explicit and limited to finishing the already-issued atomic merge readback.

findings.title: Applied merges lose canonical receipt when the command reports a transport failure
findings.body: The helper reads back the PR but then requires a zero CLI exit even if merged=true. A server-applied merge followed by a command error is an ambiguous transport outcome that must retain the error and finish merge-object/receipt readback from confirmed GitHub state, without issuing another merge.

checks_without_findings: Exact head/tree/base/repository/worktree identity checks and writer lock verification are present.
Explicit normal merge uses --match-head-commit for954; no auto/admin/squash/rebase/delete flags or main/#12 mutation.
The helper records mark-ready and merge-command outcomes before subsequent work, and checks actual merge tree/parents.
limits: Static review only; helper not executed and no merge decision produced.
Hosted CI was still running and the controller-premerge-decision file did not yet exist; their completed bindings require review before execution.
Normal GitHub merge protects the head, while the base is checked immediately around preflight and validated after merge. Controller ownership must preserve the integration base during the operation.
